_comment: Aelgard Moryskah bestiary. Moryskah is the cold-fog region: undead, vampyres, werewolves, grave-spawn. Tone is dread softened by black humor — a funeral director's gallows wit. Bibles reference wet stone, chapel ash, family debts paid in blood. See data/npc-bibles.json for cross-voiced NPCs (mirelda_bog_witch, father_dorin).
_region_tone: damp stone, perpetual dusk, undead economies. Not goth-for-goth — things rot here because the soil remembers the dead and refuses to digest them.

monsters.name: Grave-spawn
monsters.examine: Claws its way up nightly. Gives up nightly.
bible: Moryskah bodies do not stay buried; the soil is too saturated with the memory of pain. Each night, one in forty graves produces a grave-spawn: a body remembering how to claw upward but having forgotten what it wanted to do once topside.

They do not hunt. They stand in churchyards and wait. If they see a living thing they will walk toward it at a distracted pace, reach out, and stop confused at an arm's length. This pause is the only window to strike.

At dawn they lie down, sink into the soil, and the cycle begins again next dusk. Father Dorin's dawn broom-sweep of the churchyard is mostly symbolic, but the noise seems to help them find their graves.
monsters.habitat: the four Moryskah churchyards, drifting inward from the boundary fence as the night deepens
monsters.reagent_callout: Grave-spawn ichor is a Moryskah-wide crafting reagent; feeds into salted-blade combination.

monsters.name: Crypt howler
monsters.examine: Howls names. Your name is in there somewhere.
bible: A howler is a werewolf that died in a tomb and reanimated before anyone buried it properly. It still has the werewolf's nose for blood and the dead's indifference to pain. Its howl is not a warning — it is a list.

The list is names. Old Moryskah families have, for centuries, recorded the names their kin must not speak within hearing of a crypt. Violating the list calls the howler. Children get slapped for this, hard.
They can be outrun in open ground, but they do not chase; they pace. They wait for the tomb-door to be opened again. Time is on their side.
monsters.habitat: family crypts, ossuaries, the old mausoleum quarter
monsters.anti_pattern_note: do NOT let the howler run open ground. The mechanic is tomb-pacing — fight happens in a constrained crypt layout.

monsters.name: Nocturne lord
monsters.examine: Dresses for a dinner you are the main course of.
bible: A Nocturne is a vampyre grown into social confidence — it buys tailored clothes, attends the midnight opera, and keeps a bank account. Killing one triggers a probate dispute that the Moryskah notary will not resolve quickly.
They prefer to feed on inheritance — widows, recent orphans, signing parties. A Nocturne that has cornered a grieving family will often be, technically, inside the legal rights of the will.
The weakness to slash is not physical. It is that a Nocturne will not fight a blade it recognises as family silver.
monsters.habitat: Moryskah opera house, notary offices after 11pm, first-floor drawing rooms with shuttered windows
monsters.reagent_callout: Cursed signet + family silver blade = Nocturne-bane (slayer-niche vs all vampyre-tag mobs).

monsters.name: Werewolf stalker
monsters.examine: Moves sideways along the alleys. Leaves footprints pointing the wrong way.
bible: Moryskah werewolves do not live in forests. They live in terraced housing on Kettle Lane and pay rent. During the day they are bakers, coachmen, and, famously, one of the city assessors. At night, the moon finds whichever alley they are in.

A stalker is a werewolf who has slipped. The neighbours know. The landlord knows. The assessor knows. The hunt to bring one down is usually led by a cousin, wearing an apron, with the family silver dagger drawn reluctantly.

If you put the stalker down, you are expected to deliver the corpse to the family door before dawn, with your face uncovered, so the mourners can see who did it. This is the custom. Ignoring it is unwise.
monsters.habitat: residential alleys after moonrise, the coaching-house roofs, bakery backyards
monsters.anti_pattern_note: drop-off-the-corpse custom is real; skipping it is a named social debt that surfaces later.

monsters.name: Bone priest
monsters.examine: Preaches sermons to the bones. They listen.
bible: A bone priest is a priest of the Old Consent — the pre-Crown Moryskah faith that held the dead were citizens with voting rights, abolished in law but not in practice. The priest preaches to the bones of a particular ossuary, which the priest insists is 'the congregation.'

The sermons are genuinely theological, not ritual noise. You can kill a bone priest cleanly, but you interrupt what is, by every Moryskah priest-counsel ruling, a religious service. Father Dorin has written three tracts on whether this is lawful.
They carry a chapel-ash censer which, if salvaged, will cool any blade to a point a vampyre cannot ignore.
monsters.habitat: ossuaries, abandoned chapels, the crypt level of the Moryskah cathedral
monsters.reagent_callout: Chapel ash is a core Moryskah reagent; three chapel ash + any blade = salted blade (vampyre-effective).

monsters.name: Salt vampire
monsters.examine: Driven from Saltbrine. Still tastes the sea.
bible: A salt vampire is a Saltbrine-exile vampyre, cast out of its sea-coven for reasons nobody outside the coven knows or cares to hear. It retains the Saltbrine fang-hunger plus a permanent thirst — all food tastes of brine to it, including the living.
They cannot cross salt lines; Moryskah households that know one is near trace the doorway in kitchen salt every evening. Salt vampires know this and carry a grudge against cooks.
Their fang, salted and treated, is one of the few vampyre-bane crafting reagents that functions outside Moryskah.
monsters.habitat: Moryskah docklands, brine-reeking cellars, kitchens that stopped salting
monsters.reagent_callout: Salt vampire fang + ordinary stake = brined stake (doubles damage vs ALL vampyre-tag across regions).

monsters.name: Coffin crawler
monsters.examine: What gets loose when a coffin is rushed.
bible: Coffin crawlers are what emerges from coffins buried too shallow, too fast, or without the full Moryskah rites. They are spine, ribs, and a muscular crawling gait — stronger than they should be because they have no head to starve.

Moryskah undertakers are paid per depth-foot of burial, which is why shallow graves are endemic. Coffin crawlers are the tax levied on that economy. Every third month the Crown fines the cemetery a flat sum and the cycle continues.
A crawler can be stopped cleanly with a crush to the spine. A slash simply creates two smaller crawlers. The junior gravediggers carry hammers for this reason.
monsters.habitat: new-dug graves, undertaker yards, the three-month-old plots
monsters.anti_pattern_note: slash split mechanic is real — NEVER equip a slash weapon if there are multiple crawlers.

monsters.name: Fenbolter
monsters.examine: A bog-born thing that throws bones.
bible: The Moryskah fens have a unique pest: a skeletal humanoid that stands in the reeds, collects the bones of smaller things, and throws them with unnerving accuracy. A fenbolter's aim improves with the distance; at forty paces it can hit a moving cat.
They are not hostile until you enter their throwing range, which is how any fen-walker learns the range quickly. The bones they throw are not infectious, but they are exceptionally sharp.
Country wisdom: if you see a heron standing still in the Moryskah fens, there is a fenbolter within forty paces. The heron is waiting to eat something the fenbolter takes down.
monsters.habitat: Moryskah fens, reed-beds, bog edges at low tide
monsters.anti_pattern_note: the throw range telegraph is the reed stillness. Do not reveal the mob until the player crosses the forty-pace line.

monsters.name: Bog-witch acolyte
monsters.examine: A student of Mirelda's. Still learning, still dangerous.
bible: Mirelda the Bog Witch (see NPC bible) accepts two acolytes at a time: usually young Moryskah women with a grievance and a talent for herb-lore. They train for four years and, in most cases, take up practice in a neighbouring village.

An acolyte is passive unless cornered or insulted (Mirelda insists: 'never insult a woman you've bled in front of.' Her apprentices apply this broadly). They cast a limited range of bog-curses — mostly slow, misdirection, and mild decomposition.
A killed acolyte draws Mirelda's attention without exception. She remembers names. She does not punish on the same day, but she does punish.
monsters.habitat: the fens around Mirelda's cottage, the bog-path to the Heartlands border, riverbank herb patches
monsters.anti_pattern_note: killing an acolyte is a durable social penalty — surfaces in quest dialogue with Mirelda for the rest of the account.

monsters.name: Hollow hunter
monsters.examine: A ranger who killed one too many things that wanted his body.
bible: A hollow hunter is what a Moryskah game-ranger becomes when he stops sleeping. Over years of hunting crypt-emergers, the hunter loses the differences between the things he hunts and himself. He becomes 'hollow' — still a man, but with empty ribs, and a body that no longer digests.
They hunt alone, wear their old ranger greens, and carry the same bow their grandfather was buried with. They will not speak. They will aim, lower the bow, and walk past you if you are empty-handed.
The only reliable way to talk to one is to approach with your hands open and say, 'I am carrying nothing.' He will listen for one question.
monsters.habitat: Moryskah wilderness trails, deep forest ranger-paths, the foothills at dusk
monsters.reagent_callout: Drops hollow-hunter bowstring (1/64) — reagent for Hollowstring shortbow (slayer-niche vs undead-tag).

monsters.name: Rust wraith
bible: Rust wraiths form where Moryskah rain meets buried Sootworks armour — abandoned from the campaign and left to rot. The wraith is the oxidised soul of an armour-set, retaining its shape and its wearer's last grudge.
They degrade iron and steel weapons on hit. A seasoned hunter fights them with an oak cudgel. A foolish hunter fights them with family steel and loses the heirloom.
They can be compelled to a truce by offering them a single pristine iron ingot. The ingot rusts through in their grip; they are satisfied for a fortnight.
monsters.habitat: marshy battlefield remnants, where a Sootworks detachment was lost
monsters.anti_pattern_note: weapon degradation on hit is a REAL mechanic — surface the warning to the player before engage.

monsters.name: Tollhouse ghoul
bible: The Moryskah-border tollhouse has a ghoul. He is the long-dead toll-keeper, who will emerge from the cellar at any transaction, demand the toll, and if you pay, grudgingly return to the cellar.
The toll has not gone up in sixty years. A copper piece still works. The current living toll-keeper (his great-nephew) considers this a good thing and has made no effort to modernise the posted rate.

Killing the ghoul permanently closes the tollhouse as a safe stop for travellers — the nephew will relocate the office within a week. This is a lose-lose outcome. The mourning merchants tell their children.
monsters.habitat: the Moryskah-Heartlands border tollhouse cellar, emerging only for transactions
monsters.anti_pattern_note: killing the ghoul has named world-state consequences; this is not a 'free' slayer kill.

monsters.name: Lantern ghost
monsters.examine: He walks the fog with a light. He is the reason travellers survive.
bible: Moryskah fog thickens so badly at certain crossings that travellers die of simple disorientation. A lantern ghost is a good-faith ghost — a dead traveller who walked the road in life and walks it in death, carrying a light so others do not die.
They are passive and helpful. Killing one is legally murder under Moryskah Assembly Act 7 (1604 reform), and the Assembly does enforce it — the punishment is exile for seven years.
They can be asked for directions once per night per traveller. They cannot be bribed, fed, or kept as pets.
monsters.habitat: fog-crossings, the moors between Moryskah and the Wilds, the Moryskah fen at winter dusk
monsters.anti_pattern_note: passive AND helpful. Slayer tasks on them are explicitly disallowed. If a Slayer Master gives this task, it is a test and should be refused.

monsters.name: Mausoleum scholar
monsters.examine: A scholar who became a fixture of his library.
bible: Moryskah University has a mausoleum library — books so old the scholars bound to them do not leave. Over decades a full-time scholar becomes part of the collection. The transformation is gradual, mostly paper-skin and vellum-voice, and nobody is sure at what point the man becomes the footnote.
They attack trespassers who touch the wrong books. The wrong books are catalogued; the correct books are also catalogued. The catalogue is available at the front desk.
A scholar can be distracted by a citation argument. This requires the player to have read the relevant text, which requires the relevant text to still exist.
monsters.habitat: Moryskah University mausoleum library, third basement and below
monsters.reagent_callout: Drops vellum-voice scroll — reagent for the Scholar's Gambit spell (single-target silence, reagent-gated).

monsters.name: Bell hag
monsters.examine: Rings a bell you cannot hear until she rings it for you.
bible: Bell hags are Moryskah's mourners-for-hire: elderly women who attend funerals, ring a handbell, and wail on behalf of families who do not wish to. After decades in the trade, some hags grow bound to the bell-sound; they cannot be buried, and their bells ring of themselves.
At night they haunt the district they worked in. The bell-sound only carries to people marked for death by circumstances the hag alone senses. Most people never hear it.

Killing a bell hag silences the bell. This is considered a mercy by the hag's family and a civic loss by everyone else; certain funeral customers will pay well for the bell to fall silent, so there is a grey-market trade.
monsters.habitat: Moryskah mourning district, funeral homes, the bell-tower of the third chapel
monsters.anti_pattern_note: grey-market bounty exists; completing it is lore-surfacing, not just XP.

region_flavor_drops: Salt vampire fang (reagent: brined stake, vampyre-niche across ALL regions)
Hollow-hunter bowstring (1/64 — reagent: Hollowstring shortbow, undead-niche)
